title: Highest-priority critically important antimicrobial prescribing in four small-animal clinics
subtitle: QI project with PDSA cycles and weekly run charts across a veterinary group
statement: In a group of four small-animal clinics, 27 percent of systemic antimicrobial prescriptions for dogs and cats last quarter were highest-priority critically important antimicrobials (HPCIAs), mainly long-acting cefovecin injections in cats and fluoroquinolones in dogs, although the group's own guideline reserves them for cases with a culture and sensitivity result. Only 9 percent of animals treated for a suspected urinary infection had a urine culture first. The project will test whether a change package of a prescribing prompt, a consult-room guide, time-limited free urine culture and monthly clinic feedback reduces the weekly HPCIA share.
whoAffected: Dogs and cats treated in the four clinics, their owners, the 19 veterinary surgeons who prescribe, the nursing team who dispense and collect urine samples, and the wider community that relies on HPCIAs staying effective for animals and people.
whatHurts: HPCIA use without culture exposes animals to broad-spectrum drugs they may not need and selects for resistance that can pass between pets and the people they live with. Cats with idiopathic cystitis may receive an antimicrobial that cannot help them, and the options left for animals with resistant infections shrink.
currentPractice: Prescribing follows individual habit; the written guideline is not measured; cultures are rarely submitted for suspected urinary infections; long-acting injections are chosen for cats that are hard to give tablets to.
whyNow: A measured baseline of 27 percent HPCIA use, partners willing to protect monthly meeting time for feedback, and two months of budgeted free urine culture this autumn.
constraints: No external funding; all work happens in normal clinic hours. Weekly measures must come from practice management system reports without reading clinical notes. One prescribing prompt can be added by our software administrator; no other changes to the practice management system before 2027.
patientCenteredGoal: Every dog and cat that needs an antimicrobial receives the narrowest effective one, guided by culture where it matters, and owners understand why and can give it at home.
summary: Problem framed as a group-level QI project to reduce HPCIA prescribing with a change package tested in PDSA cycles.
